Intrepid

in-TREP-id -- stress on the second syllable, TREP. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Intrepid is fearless or adventurous.

The intrepid rescue pilot flew into the canyon in a crosswind that had turned back two other crews.

Worked Example

A twelve-year-old signs up to give the very first speech at the school assembly -- not because she is a natural on stage, but because somebody has to go first and nobody else will.

That is intrepid: fearless, willing to walk toward the thing others avoid. Intrepid is always admiring, and it is not the same as reckless -- an intrepid person meets real danger on purpose and with open eyes, while a reckless one never stops to look at all.

How Intrepid Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

fearless

fearless: showing no fear of danger

valiant

valiant: showing courage in the face of difficulty

dauntless

dauntless: impossible to discourage or intimidate

Antonyms

timid

timid: lacking courage; easily frightened

fearful

fearful: full of fear; afraid to act

How Strong Is It? — valiant → intrepid → dauntless

valiant vs. intrepid

valiant vs. intrepid: Valiant praises the courage inside a single act -- a valiant stand at one bridge -- while intrepid describes a settled character that keeps choosing the dangerous road, day after day.

dauntless vs. intrepid

dauntless vs. intrepid: Dauntless goes one step past intrepid: an intrepid traveler feels the fear and goes anyway, while a dauntless one cannot be discouraged at all, by any setback or any warning.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of intrepid.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: not (Latin in-)

root — trepid-

root — trepid-: fearful, trembling (Latin trepidus 'alarmed, trembling')

Put it together

Put it together: Intrepid is this unit's prefix in- ('not') on Latin trepidus ('trembling with fear'), so an intrepid person is literally 'not trembling.' Be honest about the limit: 'trepid' is not a word you can use on its own in modern English, which makes this decomposition likely rather than airtight -- but the root is alive and well in trepidation, the nervous trembling an intrepid person does not feel.

Use the root in a new word: trepidation

Use the root in a new word: trepidation: She opened the envelope with trepidation, certain it held bad news.

Root Check

Word Choice

Intrepid is a compliment, and it keeps good company: an intrepid explorer, an intrepid reporter, an intrepid rescuer. Keep it clear of reckless, which is a criticism -- an intrepid climber studies the route and then climbs it, while a reckless one climbs without ever looking at it.
